criteria: With `outputReferences: true` and `outputReferenceFallbacks: true`, a shadow token whose layers reference dimension/color tokens emits one `var(--<ref-name>, <value>)` per reference, and each fallback `<value>` is the resolved value of the token that reference points to (e.g. `var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-x, 0)`, `var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-y, 0.5rem)`, `var(--appearance-color-shadow-layer-1, rgba(71, 98, 133, 0.2))`).
No emitted fallback contains another `var(...)` — fallbacks never nest or chain through other references.

Every reference from the token's original value appears exactly once in the output at the position where its resolved value occurs, including when several references resolve to identical values (e.g. multiple `0px` dimensions across layers) — none are dropped, collapsed into each other, or moved to another layer's slot.

With `outputReferenceFallbacks` false or unset, object/array-valued tokens with references still emit the existing `var(--ref)` form unchanged (existing border/shadow reference outputs and snapshots do not change).
description:
When `outputReferences: true` is combined with `outputReferenceFallbacks: true`, composite (object/array-valued) tokens produce semantically wrong fallback chains. Reproduces with a `shadow`/`boxShadow` token whose value is an array of layers, where each layer references dimension/color tokens (reported upstream as style-dictionary issue #1602, v5.1.1).

Actual output: the first reference's fallback chains through unrelated references from other layers, e.g.
`--shadow-default: var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-x, var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-2-spread, var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-2-x, var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-2-y, 0)))) var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-y, 0.5rem) ...`

Expected: every reference emits its own fallback holding its own resolved value, in its own position:
`--shadow-default: var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-x, 0) var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-y, 0.5rem) var(--appearance-shadow-default-layer-1-blur, 1rem) ...`

Root cause: for object/array-valued tokens, `createPropertyFormatter` keeps the already-flattened transformed value string (e.g. `0 8px 16px -8px rgba(...), 0 0 1px 0 rgba(...)`) and rewrites references with `String.prototype.replace(refResolvedValue, ...)`, which replaces only the first textual occurrence. Because the fallback option inserts the resolved value into the emitted text (`var(--ref, 0)`), every later reference whose resolved value is the same (e.g. the several `0` dimensions across layers) matches inside the fallback that was just emitted, so unrelated references nest inside it instead of landing in their own slot. Without `outputReferenceFallbacks` the inserted text is just `var(--ref)`, which is why the bug only shows up with fallbacks enabled. The same mechanism can also match inside previously emitted `var()` names, so the defect is not specific to boxShadow — it affects any object/array-valued token with multiple references (shadow, border, typography, gradient).
